translation_en: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali and Muhammad ibn Abi Umar narrated to us; they used nearly identical wording. Ibn Abi Umar said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Ishaq said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Thawr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I kept wanting to ask Umar about the two wives of the Prophet concerning whom Allah Most High said, “If you two repent to Allah, for your hearts have inclined…” Quran 66:4, until Umar went on pilgrimage and I went with him. When we were on part of the road, Umar turned aside, and I went with him carrying a water container. He went to relieve himself, then came to me, and I poured water over his hands so he performed ablution. I said, “Commander of the Faithful, who are the two wives of the Prophet concerning whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, ‘If you two repent to Allah, for your hearts have inclined…’” Umar said, “How strange you are, Ibn Abbas!”—al-Zuhri said: By Allah, he disliked that he had asked him, but he did not conceal the answer—“They are Hafsah and Aishah.” Then he began relating the full account. He said: We Quraysh were a people who prevailed over our women. When we came to Medina, we found a people whose women prevailed over them, and our women began learning from their women. My home was among Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd in the highlands. One day I became angry with my wife, and she answered me back. I objected to her answering me back. She said, “Why do you object to my answering you back? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet answer him back, and one of them may stay away from him from morning until night.” I went and entered upon Hafsah and said, “Do you answer the Messenger of Allah back?” She said, “Yes.” I said, “Does one of you stay away from him from morning until night?” She said, “Yes.” I said, “Whoever among you does that has failed and lost. Does one of you feel safe that Allah might become angry with her because His Messenger is angry with her, and then she would be ruined? Do not answer the Messenger of Allah back, and do not ask him for anything. Ask me whatever you need. Do not let it deceive you that your co-wife is more beautiful and more beloved to the Messenger of Allah than you”—meaning Aishah. Umar said: I had an Ansari neighbor, and we took turns going down to the Messenger of Allah: one day he went down, and the next day I went down. He would bring me news of revelation and other matters, and I would bring him similar news. We used to hear that Ghassan was preparing its horses to attack us. My companion went down one day, then came to me in the evening and knocked at my door and called me. I went out to him. He said, “A great event has happened.” I said, “What is it? Has Ghassan come?” He said, “No, something greater and more serious: the Prophet has divorced his wives.” I said, “Hafsah has failed and lost. I had thought this might happen.” After I prayed dawn prayer, I dressed and went down to Hafsah. She was crying. I asked, “Has the Messenger of Allah divorced you?” She said, “I do not know. He is there, staying apart in this upper chamber.” I went to one of his black servants and said, “Ask permission for Umar.” He entered, then came out to me and said, “I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.” I went away until I reached the pulpit and sat down. A group of people were sitting near him, some of them weeping. I sat for a while, then what I felt overcame me. I went back to the servant and said, “Ask permission for Umar.” He entered, then came out and said, “I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.” I turned to leave, but the servant called me and said, “Come in; he has given you permission.” I entered and greeted the Messenger of Allah. He was leaning on a mat of woven palm strips that had left marks on his side. I said, “Have you divorced your wives, Messenger of Allah?” He raised his head toward me and said, “No.” I said, “Allah is the Greatest! Messenger of Allah, if you could see us: we Quraysh were a people who prevailed over our women. When we came to Medina, we found a people whose women prevailed over them, so our women began learning from theirs. One day I became angry with my wife, and she answered me back. I objected to that, and she said, ‘Why do you object to my answering you back? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet answer him back, and one of them may stay away from him from morning until night.’ I said, ‘Whoever among them does that has failed and lost. Does one of them feel safe that Allah might become angry with her because His Messenger is angry with her, and then she would be ruined?’” The Messenger of Allah smiled. I said, “Messenger of Allah, I went to Hafsah and told her, ‘Do not let it deceive you that your co-wife is more beautiful than you and more beloved to the Messenger of Allah.’” He smiled again. I said, “May I sit and keep you company, Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Yes.” I sat down and looked around the room. By Allah, I saw nothing that caught the eye except three hides. I said, “Pray to Allah, Messenger of Allah, to grant your community abundance. He has granted abundance to Persia and Rome, though they do not worship Allah.” He sat upright and said, “Are you in doubt, Ibn al-Khattab? Those are people whose good things have been hastened for them in the life of this world.” I said, “Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to forgive me.” He had sworn not to visit them for a month because of how angry he was with them, until Allah reproached him. Al-Zuhri said: Urwah informed me, from Aishah, who said: When twenty-nine nights had passed, the Messenger of Allah came to me. He began with me. I said, “Messenger of Allah, you swore not to visit us for a month, but you came after twenty-nine nights; I have been counting them.” He said, “A month can be twenty-nine days.” Then he said, “Aishah, I am going to tell you something. There is no harm if you do not hurry in deciding until you consult your parents.” Then he recited to me the verse, “O Prophet, say to your wives…” through “a great reward” Quran 33:28–29. Aishah said: By Allah, he knew that my parents would never tell me to leave him. I said, “Should I consult my parents about this? I desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Home of the Hereafter.” Ma‘mar said: Ayyub informed me that Aishah said, “Do not tell your other wives that I chose you.” The Prophet said to her, “Allah sent me to convey the message; He did not send me to make things difficult.” Qatadah said: “Their hearts have inclined” means “their hearts have turned.”
